description: Type into a session, wait for it to respond, and return the new screen (as a diff by default). The screen shows row numbers, the cursor as [x], and highlighted items as «…». text is typed first, then secret_env, then keys. Use input for interleaving, e.g. save and quit vim: input=[{key:'esc'},{text:':wq'},{key:'enter'}]. Edits that depend on where the cursor lands can go wrong when batched; prefer commands that do not (e.g. vim :2,3s/^pick/squash/) or check the screen between steps. Key names: enter, tab, esc, backspace, delete, up, down, left, right, home, end, pageup, pagedown, space, f1-f12, single characters, with ctrl+/alt+/shift+ (ctrl+c, shift+tab).

input.description: Ordered mix of text, keys, secrets and mouse events. When given, text/keys/secret_env are ignored. A mouse event clicks or scrolls at a screen row and column as numbered in the snapshot, e.g. {mouse:{action:'click',row:5,col:12}}; it only works in programs that turned on mouse input.

keys.description: Keys pressed after text, in order.

paste.description: Send text as a bracketed paste: use for multi-line input into editors and REPLs.

secret_env.description: Name of an environment variable of the tui-use server whose value is typed (e.g. a password). The value never appears in responses or recordings.

session.description: Session id (s1) or the name given to tui_start.

text.description: Text typed literally. \n is sent as Enter.

wait.description: When to return. Conditions are OR-ed. Without one, the tool waits until the screen stops changing (300 ms quiet), which is fine for most steps; use text/regex/gone for slow programs.

gone.description: Return once this substring is no longer on screen (e.g. a spinner or 'Installing').

idle_ms.description: Return after this long with no output.

regex.description: Return once this JavaScript regex matches the screen.

text.description: Return once this substring is on screen.

timeout_ms.description: Upper bound in ms. Default 5000, max 600000.

name: tui_send
